summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted for shortness of breath and alcohol intoxication. He was initially agitated and uncooperative but gradually stabilized with treatment for a COPD exacerbation, including steroids, bronchodilators, and antibiotics. He showed signs of alcohol withdrawal, requiring diazepam and supportive vitamins. His breathing improved, and oxygen needs decreased, but he continued to experience withdrawal symptoms. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave against medical advice on the fourth day, declining further monitoring or rehab referral. He was discharged on oral medications with instructions to continue treatment at home.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous
